cards.front: Recall a key point about Problem-Solving in Engineering
cards.back: Engineering problem-solving follows a systematic process: define, research, develop, test, evaluate, iterate.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Problem-Solving in Engineering
cards.back: The design brief defines the problem, requirements, constraints and criteria for success.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Problem-Solving in Engineering
cards.back: A specification translates the brief into measurable technical requirements: dimensions, materials, performance targets.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Problem-Solving in Engineering
cards.back: Research gathers information about existing solutions, materials, processes, user needs and relevant standards.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Problem-Solving in Engineering
cards.back: Ideation generates multiple possible solutions; the best are developed through sketching, modelling and calculation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Problem-Solving in Engineering
cards.back: Prototyping and testing validate design decisions: physical tests confirm that the solution meets the specification.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Problem-Solving in Engineering
cards.back: Evaluation compares the solution against the specification: does it meet all requirements? What are the trade-offs?

cards.front: Recall a key point about Problem-Solving in Engineering
cards.back: Iterative design improves the solution through repeated cycles of test, evaluate and modify.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Problem-Solving in Engineering
cards.back: Fitness for purpose means the product performs its intended function reliably under expected conditions.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Problem-Solving in Engineering
cards.back: Risk assessment identifies potential hazards, estimates likelihood and severity, and specifies control measures.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Problem-Solving in Engineering
cards.back: Systems diagrams show inputs, processes and outputs, helping engineers understand complex problems.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Problem-Solving in Engineering
cards.back: Cost-benefit analysis weighs the financial cost of a solution against the benefits it delivers.

cards.front: What should you know about gcse engineering exam tips — problem-solving in engineering?
cards.back: 1. For Problem-Solving in Engineering questions, use precise design and technology terminology 2. Consider function, aesthetics, ergonomics, sustainability and cost in your answers 3. When evaluating, justify your design decisions with reference to user needs and specifications 4. Show your understanding of Problem-Solving in Engineering through both theory and practical application 5. Reference real products and manufacturing processes where relevant

A company needs a portable tablet stand for site engineers that is stable on uneven ground, folds flat and costs under 15 pounds to manufacture. Describe the problem-solving process from brief to final design. [8 marks]

AO2 (Application): Apply knowledge and understanding of problem-solving in engineering to analyse, design and manufacture engineering solutions. AO3 (Evaluation): Evaluate engineer
